html:
Tokaji is a sweet white wine from the Tokaj region of northeastern Hungary, made from grapes shrivelled by noble rot, whose aszú style was described in the 1600s.

The grapes, mostly Furmint, are left on the vine until a mould dries them and concentrates their sugar. They are picked one by one and soaked in wine. From 1730 its vineyards were ranked by quality, one of the first such systems in the world, and a royal decree of 1737 fixed the region's borders. Tokaji was served at the courts of France, Russia and Poland, and Louis XIV is said to have called it the wine of kings and king of wines. Francis II Rákóczi sent it as a diplomatic gift. Communist collective farming hurt its quality. It is a World Heritage landscape, and the national anthem of Hungary names its vineyards.
sum: Tokaji is a sweet white wine from the Tokaj region of northeastern Hungary, made from grapes shrivelled by noble rot, whose aszú style was described in the 1600s.
